paragraphs.title: The Parable of the Poor Man’s Ewe and David’s Judgment

easy.explanation: Nathan said there were two men in one city: one rich and one poor.
easy.q: How many men were in the city Nathan described?

easy.explanation: The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds.
easy.q: What did the rich man have?

easy.explanation: The rich man took the poor man’s only ewe lamb.
easy.q: What did the rich man take from the poor man?

answers: He refused to feed the traveler
He took the poor man’s only lamb despite his own abundance
medium.explanation: The rich man had many animals but took the poor man’s beloved ewe.
medium.q: Why was David’s anger greatly kindled against the rich man?

medium.explanation: A ewe is a female sheep.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “ewe” mean?

answers: He should restore the lamb fourfold
He should give away all his animals
medium.explanation: David said the man should restore the lamb fourfold.
medium.q: What judgment did David pronounce on the rich man?

answers: He had abundant flocks and herds but took the poor man’s only lamb
The poor man had refused to help him
The traveler stole the lamb first
challenge.explanation: The rich man lacked nothing, yet he took the poor man’s only precious animal.
challenge.q: What made the rich man’s action especially unjust?

answers: It belonged to a large flock
It ate from his meat, drank from his cup, and lay in his bosom
challenge.explanation: These details show that the ewe was treated as a beloved member of the household.
challenge.q: Which detail shows the poor man’s special affection for the ewe?

answers: He recognized the wrong immediately but did not yet realize the parable concerned him
challenge.explanation: David condemned the rich man before Nathan revealed, “Thou art the man.”
challenge.q: What does David’s response to the parable reveal?

paragraphs.title: The Rebuke: You Are the Man

easy.explanation: Nathan told David that the parable pointed to him.
easy.q: To whom did Nathan say, “Thou art the man”?

answers: Anointed him king and delivered him from Saul
Given him the city of Rabbah
easy.explanation: The LORD anointed David king and delivered him from Saul.
easy.q: What had the LORD done for David?

answers: Killing Uriah and taking his wife
easy.explanation: Nathan rebuked David for killing Uriah and taking Uriah’s wife.
easy.q: What sin did Nathan charge David with committing?

answers: To show that David had received much and had no excuse for his evil
medium.explanation: The LORD had given David great blessings, making his actions even more grievous.
medium.q: Why did Nathan remind David of the blessings he had received?

answers: To treat it with contempt and disobey it
medium.explanation: Nathan said David had despised the LORD’s commandment by doing evil.
medium.q: What does it mean to despise the commandment of the LORD?

answers: The sword would never depart from his house
All his livestock would be destroyed
medium.explanation: Nathan declared, “The sword shall never depart from thine house.”
medium.q: What judgment was announced against David’s house?

answers: David acted secretly, but the LORD would bring judgment before all Israel and before the sun
David acted openly and therefore would not be punished
David had done nothing, so only Joab would be punished
challenge.explanation: The public judgment contrasted with David’s secret wrongdoing.
challenge.q: How did the announced punishment correspond to David’s secret sin?

answers: Both took something precious from another person despite having plenty
Neither had received blessings from God
challenge.explanation: The rich man took the poor man’s ewe, and David took Uriah’s wife despite his own abundance.
challenge.q: What similarity does the parable reveal between David and the rich man?

challenge.explanation: The LORD said He would raise up evil against David out of his own house.
challenge.q: Which phrase specifically connects the coming evil with David’s household?

paragraphs.title: David’s Confession and the Child’s Death

answers: I have sinned against the LORD
easy.explanation: David openly confessed, “I have sinned against the LORD.”
easy.q: What did David say after Nathan rebuked him?

easy.explanation: Nathan said, “The LORD also hath put away thy sin.”
easy.q: What did Nathan say the LORD had done with David’s sin?

easy.explanation: The child died on the seventh day.
easy.q: What happened to the child on the seventh day?

answers: He besought God, fasted, and lay upon the earth
He ate bread with his servants
medium.explanation: David prayed for the child, fasted, and lay all night upon the earth.
medium.q: How did David respond while the child was sick?

answers: The child had just been born
medium.explanation: “Very sick” describes the child’s severe illness.
medium.q: What does the KJV phrase “very sick” indicate about the child?

answers: They feared he would vex himself
They did not know whose child it was
David had already left the city
medium.explanation: They reasoned that David might harm himself if he heard the news.
medium.q: Why were David’s servants afraid to tell him that the child was dead?

answers: The LORD put away David’s sin, but the child would still die
David’s sin was not forgiven, and the child recovered
challenge.explanation: The passage presents forgiveness of David’s sin alongside the announced consequence.
challenge.q: How are forgiveness and judgment both presented in Nathan’s message?

challenge.explanation: David perceived the truth when he saw the servants whispering.
challenge.q: What caused David to realize that the child was dead?

answers: Confession, prayer and fasting, then the child’s death
The child’s death, confession, then the anointing of David
Battle, feast, confession, then the child’s birth
challenge.explanation: David confessed, sought God, fasted, and afterward the child died.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly follows the events in this passage?

paragraphs.title: David’s Response After the Child’s Death

answers: He continued lying there all day
easy.explanation: David arose from the earth after learning of the child’s death.
easy.q: What did David do after he understood that the child was dead?

easy.explanation: David came into the house of the LORD and worshipped.
easy.q: Where did David go after washing and changing his apparel?

easy.explanation: Bread was set before David, and he ate.
easy.q: What did David do when he returned to his own house?

answers: He hoped that God would be gracious and let the child live
He wanted to punish his servants
medium.explanation: David fasted and prayed in hope that God might spare the child.
medium.q: Why had David fasted while the child was alive?

answers: He cannot restore the child after death
He plans to hide the child
He will send the child into battle
medium.explanation: David recognized that death could not be reversed.
medium.q: What does David mean by “Can I bring him back again?”

answers: He understood that the child could not be brought back
His servants forced him to eat
medium.explanation: David explained that fasting could no longer change the child’s condition.
medium.q: Why did David stop fasting after the child died?

answers: He washed, anointed himself, and changed his apparel
challenge.explanation: The KJV specifically describes David washing, anointing himself, and changing his clothing.
challenge.q: What outward changes did David make after the child’s death?

answers: He turned to the LORD even after receiving the painful news
He was celebrating the child’s death
He was calling Israel to battle
challenge.explanation: David came to the house of the LORD and worshipped.
challenge.q: What does David’s worship before eating suggest?

answers: While the child lived there was hope, but after death he could not be restored
The fast was preparation for a feast
He fasted because he did not know the child
challenge.explanation: David distinguished between praying for the living child and accepting the reality of death.
challenge.q: Which statement best summarizes David’s explanation to his servants?

paragraphs.title: David Comforts Bathsheba and Solomon Is Born

easy.explanation: Bath-sheba bore a son, and David called his name Solomon.
easy.q: What was the name of the son born to David and Bath-sheba?

easy.explanation: Nathan called him Jedidiah because of the LORD.
easy.q: What additional name was given to Solomon?

medium.explanation: David went in unto Bath-sheba, and she bore a son.
medium.q: What happened after David comforted Bath-sheba?

answers: That the child was beloved of the LORD
That he was the rich man’s son
medium.explanation: The name was given because of the LORD and expresses divine love.
medium.q: What does the name Jedidiah signify in this passage?

medium.explanation: The passage says that the LORD sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet.
medium.q: Who sent Nathan to give the child the name Jedidiah?

answers: The first child died, while Solomon was born and loved by the LORD
The first child became king and Solomon went to war
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the death of the first child to the birth of Solomon, whom the LORD loved.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the first child and Solomon?

answers: The child’s association with the LORD’s love
His position as a military commander
challenge.explanation: Jedidiah was given because of the LORD and reflects divine favor.
challenge.q: What does the added name Jedidiah emphasize?

answers: David comforted Bath-sheba, Solomon was born, and the LORD loved him
Solomon was born, the first child died, and David went to battle
Nathan was born, David comforted Joab, and Solomon was anointed
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence presented in the two verses.
challenge.q: Which order of events is correct?

paragraphs.title: The Capture of Rabbah of the Ammonites

easy.explanation: Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon.
easy.q: Who fought against Rabbah at the beginning of this passage?

answers: Gather the people and capture the city
easy.explanation: Joab urged David to gather the people and complete the capture.
easy.q: What did Joab ask David to do after taking the city of waters?

easy.explanation: David took their king’s crown, which was made of gold and precious stones.
easy.q: What did David take from the king of Ammon?

answers: So the city would be called after David’s name rather than Joab’s
Because Joab did not know how to fight
So the crown could be returned
medium.explanation: Joab feared the city would be called after his own name if he captured it completely.
medium.q: Why did Joab want David to finish capturing the city?

answers: Goods taken from a conquered city
Prayer in the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: Spoil refers to valuable goods taken after victory.
medium.q: What does “spoil” mean in this passage?

answers: He fought against Rabbah and took it
He gave the city to Joab
medium.explanation: David went to Rabbah, fought against it, and captured it.
medium.q: What did David do after gathering all the people?

answers: Joab had taken the city of waters and then asked David to complete the capture of Rabbah
The city of waters was taken after David returned to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Joab reported taking the city of waters and urged David to finish the larger conquest.
challenge.q: How were the city of waters and Rabbah related in the campaign?

answers: The Israelites won and captured royal treasure
The city was abandoned before the battle
challenge.explanation: The crown and abundant spoil were taken after the city was captured.
challenge.q: What does taking the king’s crown show about the outcome of the battle?

challenge.explanation: The passage concludes, “So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.”
challenge.q: Where did David and all the people go at the end of the passage?
